conclusion: The Erdos #126 scout's mathematics survives adversarial audit: the inverse g(k) reformulation, the positivity equivalence, the Fekete/composition refutation and the whole finite table are correct, and the table reproduces exactly under an independently written search. Its omitted-prime loose thread is false (refuted by a row of its own table), its 'optima are tiny' mystery is explained by S-unit scaling, and its 'no progress beyond 1934' framing hides three relevant papers it cites none of.
confidence: High on everything re-proved by hand (sections 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 of RESULTS.md are elementary proofs a referee can check in minutes) and on the reproduced table (a second implementation, written from the problem statement, agreeing on all seven rows). Medium on the literature section: it rests on the erdosproblems.com page fetched today plus web-search summaries of Gyory-Stewart-Tijdeman 1986 and Erdos-Stewart-Tijdeman 1988 whose abstracts I did not read at source, so treat the exact constants (1/8+eps, exp(c sqrt(s)/log s)) as needing one confirmation before quoting. The S-unit reduction in section 7 is proved; the counting step built on it is explicitly not.

core_candidates.what: a 'reproduce the peer arm independently' habit for audit runs: write the search from the problem statement, never from the audited probe
core_candidates.why_reusable: it caught a real class of failure in this run. Our first implementation built the adjacency bitset one-directionally and returned max clique 1 on every row, which is obviously broken; the same bug shape returns 5 where the truth is 6 and is not obviously broken. An audit that imports the audited code cannot see either.
core_candidates.first_step: make it a line in the red-team brief template: the audit arm reimplements, it does not import

core_candidates.what: a literature-first gate on any hunt that asserts 'no progress since <year>'
core_candidates.why_reusable: the scout asserted a 92-year wall and cited no paper. One page fetch plus one search found the authoritative status, the prize, the trivial construction that benchmarks the whole finite arm, and three relevant papers including one from February 2026. Cost was under five minutes.
core_candidates.first_step: require any hunt claiming a literature state to name its source in RESULTS.md, per the AGENTS.md original-vs-novel rule

notes_for_operator: The scout was a good run and this audit does not overturn it. What it does overturn is one thread and one framing, and the cheapest lesson is the literature one: the trivial 1934 construction g(k) >= (p_k+1)/2 was the natural benchmark for the scout's entire finite table and cost one page fetch to find. Nothing here bears on RH (docs/08).
